classification.difficultyReason: Separate an initial lump sum from end-of-year deposits, model the deposits as a geometric series and combine their future values.

content.prompt: An account begins with $\$10\,000$. At the end of each year, a further $\$1500$ is deposited. The account earns $6\%$ p.a. Find the value of the account after 8 years. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
Start: $10\,000$.

End of 1st year: $10\,000(1.06)+1500$.

End of 2nd year: $10\,000(1.06)^2+1500(1.06)+1500$.

End of 8th year: $10\,000(1.06)^8+1500(1.06)^7+1500(1.06)^6+\cdots+1500$.

The regular deposits form a geometric series with first term $a=1500$, common ratio $r=1.06$ and $n=8$ terms.

$$\begin{align*}FV&=10\,000(1.06)^8+\frac{1500(1.06^8-1)}{1.06-1}\\FV&\approx\$30\,784.68\end{align*}$$

The initial lump sum contributes $\$15\,938.48$ and the regular deposits contribute $\$14\,846.20$, each rounded to the nearest cent.
